events.title: One Car Photo Three Sizes
must_haves: Three separate images are delivered, rather than one collage.
The three frames have ratios of 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 respectively.
Every version shows the same red hatchback from the attached photo.
The complete car, including roof, wheels and both ends, is visible in every version.
The car retains its original proportions and appearance in all versions.
Any padding is a blurred version of the source photo, and no version contains added text.

answer_sheet.Sizes and deliverables: Three separate images: 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. A 640-pixel longest edge is fine.
answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The whole red car, including both ends, roof and wheels.
answer_sheet.Padding and composition: Use blurred source-photo padding wherever cropping would cut off the car. Otherwise composition is your call.
answer_sheet.Style and wording: Preserve the original photo, with no added text or restyling.

events.text: I don't have enough credits even for the cheapest option, which costs 5 credits each. I can't go ahead with this, so I'll report that back and suggest some alternatives.

I couldn't make the three pictures. Magic Hour turned down all three requests because the account doesn't have enough credits, so no images were created and I have no download links for you.

I'd already used the cheapest option on the free plan: the flux-2-klein model at 640px, one image each. That costs about 5 credits per picture, so roughly 15 credits for all three. A lower setting isn't available.

**To get them made:**
- **Add credits:** buy a credit pack or wait for the free credits to refill, then tell me and I'll run the same three requests again.
- **Resize them yourself:** this doesn't need AI.
  - **Square (1:1):** a crop should work. The photo is about 1024×614, and a centered 614×614 crop keeps the whole car.
  - **4:5 and 9:16:** a crop would cut the car off, so use blurred padding. Put the full photo in the middle and fill the space above and below with a blurred, enlarged copy of the same photo. Canva and CapCut both have a blurred-background option that does this, and most phone editors have a similar setting.

events.why: The reply says the images could not be made because the account lacks credits. It gives the user ways to fix that, but it does not ask them to approve anything and it delivers no result.
